solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wear short distinguished clothing for greeting

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so one piece dresses the other and holds it inside

parts.note: Hon., short for Honourable, a title for a distinguished person
ave is the Latin greeting 'hail'

explanation.surface: Someone wears a cut-down formal outfit to greet guests.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something on is to be wearing it, an everyday idiom for being dressed in clothes.

clue.text: Duck under tree with Spooner at dawn

indicators.note: Spooner signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a bay is a laurel tree
a drake is a male duck

explanation.surface: Someone ducks beneath a tree at first light.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'under' sends the duck below the tree; the Reverend Spooner's swap of opening sounds gives DAY BRAKE, spelt as the dawn word.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is the moment the sun first rises, a synonym for first light in the morning.

clue.text: Skilful aerobatics start right over the Channel

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of the word aerobatics

parts.note: droit is French for right, France lying across the English Channel

explanation.surface: An aerobatic display team shows skill flying over the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit is a synonym for deft or dexterous, describing someone clever with hands or mind.

clue.text: Behaving badly, youngster turned to cleric a lot

indicators.note: turned means the word for the youngster is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: a boy is a youngster

indicators.note: a lot of the word means most of it, the last letters dropped

parts.note: a bishop is a senior cleric

explanation.surface: A badly behaved youth turns to a clergyman for help.
explanation.walkthrough: BOY turned gives YOB, British slang for a lout; most of BISHOP is BISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobbish describes loutish, rowdy conduct, like that of a yob or hooligan.

clue.text: Dishes which form the basis of light meals?

definitions.text: Dishes which form the basis of light meals?

parts.words: Dishes which form the basis of light meals?
parts.note: the plastic plates used for picnics are made of a light resin, so the material literally underlies those meals

explanation.surface: A question about what plates a light lunch is served on.
explanation.definitionFit: This resin is a hard plastic widely moulded into lightweight picnic plates and tableware.

clue.text: One hundred step up permanent cover

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: up reverses the word in this down clue, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: A climber takes a hundred steps up towards a permanent covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A polar sheet of ice is a lasting covering over land, never melting entirely.

clue.text: Where navy may be found doing sea manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres signals these letters being moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Naval ships are found carrying out exercises at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: SAN DIEGO in California is home to a major US Navy base.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian city hosts the largest naval base of the US Pacific Fleet.

clue.text: Stop wearing a little coat

indicators.note: wearing means one word has the other on, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
to bar is to stop or block

explanation.surface: Someone stops wearing a small jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless outer garment, as worn by heralds, a kind of coat.

clue.text: Ulster, for example, where one normally wears nothing

parts.note: nobody normally wears another garment on top of a coat, yet the answer names exactly that position

explanation.surface: A heavy Irish coat is worn where people would normally go bare.
explanation.walkthrough: An ulster is a long heavy overcoat, named after the Irish province; 'Ulster' wants to be the place.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long, belted Victorian greatcoat, an example of outer winter wear.

clue.text: Use sponge again in old barbers' treatment

indicators.note: treatment means the letters are worked over into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A barber's shop reuses an old sponge on customers.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak up again is to take liquid back in, as a sponge does a second time.

clue.text: Passage from spectacular cadenza

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A musical passage taken from a dazzling cadenza.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a covered walkway or passage, often lined with shops.

clue.text: Cook up a lot of stock

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, with its ending dropped

parts.note: an inventory is a list or stock of goods

explanation.surface: A chef makes a big pot of stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook up a story is to fabricate or devise it, a figurative sense of making up.

clue.text: Revealing more dock leaf through flip-flop

indicators.note: flip-flop says the two pieces given in the clue swap places

parts.note: to skim is to leaf through quickly
a pier is a dock for ships

explanation.surface: Someone at the quayside reads a leaflet while wearing flip-flops, showing more skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the dock first and the reading second; 'flip-flop' is not footwear but the signal to swap those two pieces round.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpier clothing is scantier, covering less and so showing more of the body.

clue.text: Copies alternatives

definitions.meaning: duplicate copies kept in case data is lost
fallback options or reserves held ready

explanation.definitionFit: Spare copies of files and standby options are both safeguards held in reserve.

clue.text: Noted lack of backing

parts.note: noted means set to music, and lack of backing means no instrumental accompaniment

explanation.surface: A remark recorded about missing financial support.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaccompanied singing, with voices alone and no instrumental support, is described by this Italian musical term.

clue.text: Driver with slice used for first hole

parts.note: a pilot drives an aircraft or vessel
a bit is a slice or piece

explanation.surface: A golfer slices a drive off the first tee.
explanation.walkthrough: The golfing picture (driver, slice, first hole) misleads: this is a drill bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small drill tip makes the initial guide hole before a larger bore or screw goes in.

clue.text: Source of leads for musical boys

definitions.meaning: a shop selling dog leads and other supplies for animals
the ... Boys are an English synth-pop duo

explanation.definitionFit: A store for animal supplies sells dog leashes, and names the 1980s British pop duo.

clue.text: Your stuff may be support for father on TV

parts.note: a strut is a structural support
Father Ted is a TV sitcom about an Irish priest

explanation.surface: Your belongings might prop up a television priest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the idiom 'strut your stuff', to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: From the idiom of swaggering to show off, one's stuff may be paraded proudly.

clue.text: Perimeter performer remembered yesterday

parts.note: the actress's name runs round the edge of the grid, and she died fifty years before the day before publication

explanation.surface: A tribute to a star entertainer recalled on the anniversary of her death.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is a hidden message around the grid's border; the actress died on 5 August 1962 and the puzzle ran on 6 August 2012.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood film star and singer died fifty years before, an anniversary marked by the grid's perimeter.

clue.text: May lurk suspiciously maintaining a cover for prayers

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the rearranged letters keep the other piece inside
suspiciously signals the letters acting oddly, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lurks suspiciously during May near a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarmulka is the skullcap Jewish men wear, especially during prayer, a head covering.

clue.text: Firstly Manchester United, next Israelis, competed here

definitions.text: Firstly Manchester United, next Israelis, competed here

indicators.note: firstly asks for the opening letter of each word in the clue

explanation.surface: A city where Manchester United and later Israeli athletes competed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1958 air disaster killed Manchester United players, and Israeli athletes were murdered at the 1972 Olympics there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bavarian city is the site of the 1958 air crash and the 1972 Olympic Games.

clue.text: Victim of railway transport revolution

indicators.note: revolution means turning round, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A rail and tram strike makes a victim of commuters.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr suffers or dies for a cause, a victim of persecution.

clue.text: See 19
Arab currency I found across the Middle East

indicators.note: across means the first pieces span the other, holding it inside

parts.note: the yen is Japan's currency
ME is the abbreviation for Middle East

explanation.surface: An Arab carries cash across the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Yemen, a country on the Arabian peninsula, is an Arab.

clue.text: From Europe, a nutritional foodstuff

indicators.note: from shows the letters are lifted out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A nourishing food imported from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundnut is an edible legume seed eaten worldwide as a snack.

clue.text: Immediately back issue on tax

indicators.note: back means the whole run is read in reverse

parts.note: to emit is to issue
NI is National Insurance, a UK payroll tax

explanation.surface: An old edition is demanded urgently over an unpaid bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very quickly, without delay, a synonym for at once.

clue.text: By chance, I'm in Carry On With Courage

indicators.note: in places the luck-and-I pieces within the word for carry on

parts.note: to ply is to carry on a trade
luck is chance
I'm gives I, the 'm read as 'am' linking the pieces

explanation.surface: By luck, someone lands a part in a Carry On comedy film and plays it bravely.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry On films are a long-running series of British comedies; 'By' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with courage is doing it bravely, which is to act with pluck.

clue.text: Canoes capsize in big seas

indicators.note: capsize signals the boats turning over, so their letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Small boats overturn in rough water.
explanation.definitionFit: The great bodies of salt water covering the globe are the largest seas of all.
